key_findings.value: For the Ni-containing 28Mn5Ni alloy, heat treatment at 873 K after 50% cold reduction increased the bulk hardness to 500 VHN, the highest among the heat-treatment temperatures investigated.

measurement_conditions.value: Peak load 30 kg (~300 N), dwell time 15 s, per ASTM E-140-02; value averaged over ten measurements on the sample

purpose.value: To evaluate the change in mechanical properties (hardness) of the cold rolled 28Mn5Ni alloy upon heat treatment in the range 873-1273 K

source.reason: Block b0022 describes the Vickers hardness method (ASTM E-140-02, AFFRI tester, 30 kg, 15 s), block b0045 reports the hardness-vs-treatment-temperature behaviour, and block b0046 gives the 873 K hardness value for 28Mn5Ni.

processing_steps_notes.value: Sound portion of the 30 kg vacuum-induction-melted ingot of the 28Mn5Ni alloy was homogenized at 1423 K for 2.5 h.

source.reason: Block b0015 describes the homogenization step of the ingot prior to hot rolling for all three LDS grades including 28Mn5Ni.

processing_steps_notes.value: Hot rolled at 1323 K; final hot-rolled plate thickness ~13 mm. This condition is hereafter referred to as HR. Details of hot rolling reported elsewhere [21].

source.reason: Block b0015 states the homogenized ingot was hot rolled at 1323 K to a final thickness of ~13 mm (condition HR).

processing_steps_notes.value: Hot-rolled plates were cold rolled at room temperature in several passes to ~50% reduction in thickness (~6 mm thick sheets); denoted HR+CR. 15Mn5Ni cracked beyond 50%, so reduction was restricted to 50% for all alloys.

source.reason: Block b0015 states samples were cold rolled to ~50% reduction in thickness at room temperature by several passes; the cold rolled samples are denoted HR+CR.

processing_steps_notes.value: Cold rolled sheet heat treated at 873 K for 1 h followed by water quenching; this specific 873 K condition defines the present sample. This is the lowest temperature of the 873-1273 K heat treatment range and is documented for hardness only.

source.reason: Block b0015 states the cold rolled sheets were heat treated in the range 873 K-1273 K for 1 h followed by water quenching; block b0046 specifically reports the hardness after heat treatment at 873 K for the 28Mn5Ni alloy.

other_conditions.value: Bulk Vickers hardness under a peak load of 30 kg (~300 N) with a dwell time of 15 s; values averaged over ten measurements on each sample.

source.reason: Block b0022 gives the hardness test standard and parameters (ASTM E-140-02, AFFRI Vickers tester, 30 kg / ~300 N peak load, 15 s dwell, average of ten measurements).

Block b0046 states that upon heat treatment at 873 K, the hardness of the Ni-containing alloys (28Mn5Ni and 15Mn5Ni) increased to 500 VHN; Fig. 8b plots the ~873 K point of the Ni-containing alloys as the highest, just below 500 VHN.

The only mechanical property reported for the 28Mn5Ni (Ni-containing) alloy after 0.5 cold reduction + heat treatment at 873 K is bulk Vickers hardness, reported as increasing to 500 VHN in block b0046 and plotted in Fig. 8b.

unmapped_findings: The 873 K heat-treatment condition of the 28Mn5Ni alloy is documented for hardness only; EBSD/OIM, XRD and TEM microstructural characterization was performed at 973 K, 1023 K and 1173 K, so no microstructure (recrystallization fraction, grain size, B2/κ-carbide fraction) is reported specifically for this 873 K sample.

Upon subsequent heat treatment at 873 K after 50% cold reduction, the hardness of the Ni-containing 28Mn5Ni alloy was increased to 500 VHN, while the Ni-free 28Mn0Ni alloy showed no noticeable change in hardness at this temperature.

In Fig. 8b the ~873 K data point is the highest of the Ni-containing series (just below 500 VHN); error bars are shown for the 28Mn5Ni (red circle) series but no numeric uncertainty for the 873 K value is tabulated.

The paper attributes the variation in hardness of the LDS alloys as a function of heat treatment temperature to precipitation and dissolution of secondary phases (κ-carbides and B2 particles) together with recrystallization and grain growth phenomena, depending on alloy composition.

As context for this sample's precursor HR+CR state, all three alloys (including 28Mn5Ni) saturated at around 450 VHN at 50% cold reduction, and the HR-condition hardness of 28Mn5Ni was reported as ~268 +/- 5 VHN [21].
